title: Gift Wrap Roll

drivers.name: Halloween event
drivers.evidence: Historical x2.04 vs baseline, but noise-adjusted x1.0; only 2 prior occurrences; no confidence in uplift.

drivers.name: Price increase (+3.4%)
drivers.evidence: Price rose to $5.72; past week at same price sold 6 units (x1.88 vs baseline), suggesting price sensitivity; no promotion, so lift unlikely.

drivers.name: Store closure (Mon)
drivers.evidence: One day lost; past closure weeks not observed, but store-wide data shows ~20% reduction in weekly sales during closures.

adjustment.analysis: Halloween (event week) has historically lifted sales to x2.04 vs baseline, with a noise-adjusted estimate of x1.0—too weak to trust. However, the target week has a price increase of +3.4% (to $5.72), which is higher than past promotions (max 30% off), and store closure on Monday reduces available sales days. The recent week with $5.72 price (2026-10-05) sold 6 units (x1.88 vs baseline), suggesting price increase may dampen demand. No promotion is scheduled, and past post-promo weeks show x0.84 (noise-adjusted x1.0), but no prior post-Halloween week exists. The baseline trend is rising (trend_13=34%), and the product is seasonal (mean_52=6.3), but the target week is after peak. Adjust cautiously: price increase and closure likely reduce demand, while Halloween has weak evidence. Final multiplier shrunk toward 1.0.

brief:
PRODUCT: Gift Wrap Roll | category Seasonal | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-10-26 to 2026-11-01 (3 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: Holiday: Halloween (Sat)
  shelf price: 5.72 (+3.4% vs regular price 5.53)
  planner notes: Store closed Monday for renovation

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 3.2 | 5%-95%: 0.0 - 10.2 | 10%-90%: 0.0 - 8.8

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-95% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
